title: Memory mosaic: kernel matching and prefill orchestration for fragmented KV residency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Investigate and implement an orchestrator that matches kernels to fragmented KV page mosaics at prefill time, reducing decode stalls and lowering 95th-percentile prefill latency for paged attention workloads. The goal is to coordinate allocation, compaction hints, and kernel selection so that fragmented residency patterns are served with kernel placements that minimize cross-page decode churn.
background: We see recurring tail-latency events when long-context workloads touch fragmented KV pages that are scattered across GPU memory. Kernels optimized for contiguous memory or microshard layouts perform poorly when pages are fragmented, causing repeated prefill reorders and decode backpressure. Existing heuristics select kernels based on average sequence length and tenant weight; they don't consider fragmentation topology or prefill window alignment.
motivation: Lower end-to-end token latency for multi-tenant paged-attention by making kernel selection fragmentation-aware and by scheduling prefill/decoder waves to favor locality. This should reduce overall GPU memory thrashing, avoid kernel-induced stalls, and improve throughput under mixed workloads without increasing average cost.
proposal_summary: Build a lightweight 'memory mosaic' profiler, extend the kernel selector to accept fragmentation fingerprints, and add a prefill orchestrator that orders decode waves to prioritize compactable page groups. The orchestrator will emit placement hints to the allocator and optionally trigger opportunistic micro-coalescing before heavy decodes.
technical_design:
- Fingerprinting: compute a compact fragmentation fingerprint per KV segment (tile occupancy bitmap compressed to 64 bits).
- Kernel capability matrix: annotate each kernel variant with preferred topologies (contiguous, microshard, sparse) and expected performance multipliers for mismatch scenarios.
- Matching algorithm: cost-based scoring combining fingerprint match, expected kernel throughput, and prefill window deadline. Use lightweight integer math so selection is <1us per request.
- Orchestration: group pending prefill requests into short-time buckets (2-5ms) and order decode waves to maximize contiguous-page utilization. If grouping can't be improved, schedule lower-priority requests on fallback kernels.
- Allocation feedback: allocator exposes soft-compact hints to begin background micro-coalescing when hotspot fragmentation is observed.
- Telemetry: expose metrics for fingerprint entropy, kernel-mismatch discount, prefill reorder rate, and per-tenant tail-latency delta.
experiments_and_results:
- Microbenchmark v1 (simulated fragmentation workload): 95th prefill latency reduced from 78ms to 46ms with memory-mosaic orchestration + contiguous-preferring kernel.
- End-to-end litmus test on mixed PLG traffic: median latency unchanged, p95 decode time down 20%, token throughput +6% under 75% load.
- Resource cost: small CPU overhead (<1% core per GPU worker) and temporary spike in background memcpy during opportunistic compaction (controlled by threshold).
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Complexity: adds more signals to kernel selection which may increase maintenance surface.
- Compaction cost: aggressive micro-coalescing can increase device-to-device copies and temporarily increase jitter. We mitigate with hysteresis and budgeted compaction windows.
- Fairness: reordering prefill waves could delay lower-priority tenants; enforce tenant-weighted arbitration and SLA bounds.
implementation_steps: Add fragmentation fingerprint generation to KV allocator and make it emitted in metadata during prefill admission
Extend kernel registry with topology preference fields and a small performance lookup table
Implement the matching algorithm in the request router and add micro-batching buckets for prefill ordering
Expose allocator soft-compact API and implement a budgeted micro-coalescer as a background task
Add metrics and tracing spans for matching decisions and prefill wave ordering
Run staged canary on dedicated pool and measure p95/p99 across workloads
acceptance_criteria: P95 prefill latency reduced by >=25% on benchmark fragmentation workload
Kernel mismatch rate (requests serviced by non-preferred kernel) reduced by >=40% for high-fragmentation segments
No increase in median latency >5% for control workloads
Background compaction budget respected: <2% GPU bandwidth increase over 5-minute windows
Telemetry dashboard populated and alerts for regression in p99 prefill latency
decisions: Use 64-bit compressed bitmap for fingerprinting (balance of entropy vs space)
Prefetch grouping window set to 3ms for initial rollout; will tune in canary
Fallback kernels remain available; do not block requests for compaction
Budgeted micro-coalescing implemented as best-effort with tenant-weighted limits
open_questions: Optimal fingerprint size for long-tail models where page fragmentation is highly variable
Whether to surface fragmentation hints to customers (privacy/abstraction concerns)
Interaction with autoscaler: compaction can change memory pressure signals—how to avoid scaling thrash
